The Finance (No. 2) Act 2010 was a significant piece of UK tax legislation that received Royal Assent on July 27, 2010. Here's what I know about it:

## Background and Context
- This was one of the first major tax acts passed by the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government that came to power in May 2010
- It followed the Finance Act 2010, which had been passed by the previous Labour government
- The act implemented various tax measures as part of the new government's fiscal policy agenda

## Key Provisions

### Income Tax Changes
- Increased the personal allowance for income tax
- Made adjustments to income tax rates and bands
- Introduced measures affecting higher-rate taxpayers

### Capital Gains Tax
- Significantly increased Capital Gains Tax rates from a flat rate of 18% to 18% for basic rate taxpayers and 28% for higher-rate taxpayers
- This was one of the most notable changes in the act

### Corporation Tax
- Included provisions relating to corporate taxation
- Made changes to various corporate tax reliefs and allowances

### Anti-Avoidance Measures
- Introduced several anti-tax avoidance provisions
- Strengthened rules around tax planning schemes

### Other Tax Changes
- Modified various aspects of inheritance tax, stamp duty, and other taxes
- Updated tax administration procedures

## Significance
The act was part of the coalition government's broader strategy to address the UK's fiscal deficit while attempting to maintain economic growth during the post-2008 financial crisis recovery period.
